newsitem.title: USA: Dow edges higher after wild swings on program trades.
newsitem.headline: Dow edges higher after wild swings on program trades.

text.p: Stocks edged higher Friday after two days of sharp declines as the market fluctuated wildly in response to a rapid series of computerized programme trades.
Right from the opening bell, the Dow Jones industrial average charted a frenzied course, sliding more than 50 points only to reverse course and surge to a 40-point increase not long after.
The swings led the NYSE to take the unusual step of imposing and lifting programme trading curbs within a span of seven minutes.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow was up 7.31 points at 6,311.02. In the broader market, losers outpaced gainers by 15 to eight on heavy volume of 255 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 10.52 points to 1,287.81.
"There's no question this is one of those very guarded, edgy rallies (in the Dow)," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.

Analysts cited a flurry of programme trading for the volatility. Birinyi Associates, which tracks programme trades, counted a total of four early Friday, three on the buy side and one on the sell side.
As a result, stocks were subject to wild swings, leading analysts to caution smaller investors to wait out the storm.
"On a day like this, individuals are better off heading for the sidelines, Johnson said. "There are a lot of very active hedge funds and proprietary trading accounts today."
For the first time in several sessions, the bond market proved to be a source of good news for stocks.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose half a point, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, to 6.59 percent from 6.62 percent at Thursday's close.

"After a little rough period this morning, bonds picked up," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "But for now things are going to be extremely choppy and there is more volatility to come when we approach options expiration next week."
Broad market indicators were mostly negative. The NYSE Composite index fell 0.87 point to 383.42, and the American Stock Exchange index fell 3.32 to 575.79.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks fell 1.60 to 727.73.

Among individual issues, Quaker Oats Co. rose 1-1/2 to 37-5/8 on speculation that it might shed its struggling Snapple beverage business as well as its Gatorade business. The company declined to comment.

Interlink Computer Sciences Inc. jumped 3-1/16 to 14-3/4 after the company formed a software development alliance with Cisco Systems Inc. Cisco fell 1 to 64-3/4, a decline in line with many other large cap technology stocks Friday.

Oracle Corp. fell 3-1/4 to 44 a day after the company reported slightly lower-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings. Cowen & Co., which had previously strongly recommended buying Oracle, downgraded it to buy. But several other firms reiterated their buy ratings on the shares.
